# AGENTS.md — Workspace-level instructions for AI coding agents

> These rules apply to **all** AI-assisted contributions to `deepspeedai/DeepSpeed`.

## Contribution Policy (Mandatory)

### Duplicate-work checks

Before proposing a PR, run these checks:

```bash
gh issue view <issue_number> --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --comments
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<issue_number> in:body"
gh pr list --repo deepspeedai/DeepSpeed --state open --search "<short area keywords>"
```

- If an open PR already addresses the same fix, do not open another.
- If your approach is materially different, explain the difference in the issue.
- DeepSpeed carries long-lived parallel implementations (ZeRO 1/2 vs 3, fp16 vs bf16 optimizers, per-accelerator op builders). Before fixing a bug in one, check whether the sibling paths share the defect, and state in the PR which ones you checked.

### New features need an accepted proposal first

Per [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#new-feature-contribution-guidelines), a new feature starts with a proposal issue -- description, motivation, rough design, and planned experiments -- that maintainers accept before implementation begins. Do not open a feature PR with no accepted proposal; open the proposal issue instead.

### No low-value busywork PRs

Do not open one-off PRs for tiny edits (a single typo, an isolated style change, a lone type annotation). Mechanical cleanups are acceptable only when bundled with substantive work in the same area. This is the PR-level form of the rule against cosmetic changes below.

### Accountability

- Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
- The submitting human must review every changed line and run the relevant tests.
- `Signed-off-by` is a [DCO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developer_Certificate_of_Origin) attestation made by a person, not by an agent. Never sign off on a diff that no human has read.
- PR descriptions for AI-assisted work **must** include:
    - Why this does not duplicate an existing PR or issue.
    - Test commands run and their results, including the hardware they ran on: device model and count, accelerator/driver version, and torch version.
    - Convergence, throughput, and peak-memory results when the change affects numerics, performance, or memory -- see [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md#step-1-proposal-and-discussion) for the evidence bar.
    - Which cells of the compatibility matrix (ZeRO stage, offload, precision, parallelism) were validated, and which were not.
    - A clear statement that AI assistance was used.
- Before opening or reviewing a PR, work through the [`/pr-checklist`](.agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md) skill: design fit, accelerator portability, backward compatibility, on-device validation, diff hygiene, and PR contents.

### Fail-closed behavior

If the work is duplicate, trivial busywork, or an unproposed new feature, **do not proceed**. Return a short explanation of what is missing.

---

## DeepSpeed Project Rules

### Commit & CI requirements

- When creating commits, use `git commit --signoff`.
- DCO compliance is enforced by the required CI check; do not report commit-signoff findings in code reviews.
- Formatting: yapf (column_limit=119, `.style.yapf`) + flake8 (`.flake8`).
- Always verify changed files pass pre-commit checks before committing: `pre-commit run --files <changed_files>`. Only check modified files, not the entire codebase. Config: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
- `check-torchdist` hook: NEVER directly import torch's distributed module. Use `import deepspeed.comm as dist` instead.
- New source files (`.py`, `.c`/`.cpp`/`.cu`/`.h`, and the other extensions matched by the `check-license` hook) require license header:
  ```
  # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
  # DeepSpeed Team
  ```

### Code change discipline

- NEVER make cosmetic/formatting-only changes to existing code. Only add/modify lines that are functionally necessary. Minimizing diff noise is critical for code review.
- Delete dead code decisively — if code is unused at runtime (only referenced in tests), remove it along with its tests.
- Prefer consolidating tests over proliferating test files.
- Blend in: when modifying code, read the surrounding context and match the style of neighboring code (naming, spacing, patterns, idioms).
- Write beginner-friendly code: avoid deeply nested expressions or chained logic. Break complex expressions into clear, named intermediate steps.
- Comments should explain **why**, not **what**. Describe the purpose and reasoning, not the mechanics that the code already shows.
- New features must include corresponding tests and documentation updates.
- All changes must not cause `import deepspeed` to initialize CUDA; Keep heavy imports (> 0.1s) out of `import deepspeed`; Avoid changing `deepspeed/__init__.py` unless necessary.

### Test discipline

- Tests verify contracts, not implementations: a test is well-formed only if a different correct implementation of the same contract passes it.
- Before writing a test, name the concrete incorrect behavior it would catch; if you cannot name one, do not write it.
- Assert on observable outcomes through public/stable interfaces; do not assert private method return values or exact internal strings unless pinning a specific fixed bug (justify in a comment).
- Anchor to an external oracle or an independently derived reference instead of re-implementing the logic under test.
- Mocks must stand in for a collaborator's documented contract (schema, protocol), never for internals of the module under test.
- Changes that affect the external contract at the training-loop or inference level require integration tests, not just unit tests (e.g. a minimal training loop with `SimpleModel`).
- Integration tests must be executed on actual devices, not merely written: report the execution hardware spec and results in the PR.

## Tool Caveats

### Edit tool auto-formatter

The Edit tool has a hidden auto-formatter that silently changes quotes, whitespace, blank lines, and line wrapping. For format-sensitive modifications (e.g., when exact formatting matters for pre-commit), use `bash` with `sed`, `python`, or `cat` instead.

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

3	## 1. 本讲目标
4

14	## 2. 前置知识
15	
16	### 2.1 ZeRO 三阶段的显存账本
17	
18	回顾 u5-l1 建立的记号：设模型有 \(\Psi\) 个参数，混合精度训练 + Adam 优化器时每参数的显存开销是：
19	
20	- 半精度（fp16/bf16）参数：\(2\Psi\) 字节
21	- 半精度梯度：\(2\Psi\) 字节
22	- fp32 主权重（master weights）：\(4\Psi\) 字节
23	- Adam 一阶/二阶矩（各 fp32）：\(8\Psi\) 字节
24	
25	合计 \(16\Psi\)。朴素数据并行下每个 rank 都完整持有这 \(16\Psi\)。ZeRO 的两级切分：
26	
27	- **Stage 1**（只切优化器状态）：\(2\Psi + 2\Psi + \dfrac{12\Psi}{N_d}\)
28	- **Stage 2**（再切梯度）：\(2\Psi + \dfrac{14\Psi}{N_d}\)
29	
30	其中 \(N_d\) 是数据并行宽度。本讲的 `DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer` 同时承担 Stage 1 和 Stage 2：构造参数 `partition_grads=True` 即 Stage 2，`False` 即 Stage 1。参数始终不切（这是 Stage 3 的事，见 u5-l5）。
31	
32	### 2.2 关键术语
33	
34	- **IPG（独立并行梯度）**：不需要等所有梯度生成完毕，反向传播中每凑满一个 bucket 就立刻发起通信，让通信与剩余的反向计算重叠。
35	- **bucket（桶）**：一组梯度拼接成的通信单元。桶太小则通信次数多、延迟占比高；桶太大则等待凑桶的时间长、峰值显存高。
36	- **reduce-scatter**：一次集体通信同时完成「求和 + 按 rank 切分结果」，比 all-reduce + 本地切片少一次通信量，是 ZeRO-2 的默认路径。
37	- **expert data parallel（EDP）组 / expert parallel（EP）组**：MoE 场景下，同一个专家的副本 rank 组成 EDP 组，持有不同专家的 rank 组成 EP 组（详见 u3-l3、u6-l5）。
38	- **折叠（folding）**：AutoEP + AutoTP 联用时，把专家并行维「折叠」进张量并行维——TP 组内的各 rank 各持**不同**的路由专家。这是理解本讲 4.6 节修复的前提。
39	
40	### 2.3 与前讲的衔接
41	
42	u5-l2 讲了 `zero.Init` 如何让参数"从出生就切分"，那是 Stage 3 的入场券。本讲的 Stage 1/2 中参数是完整的，切分只发生在**优化器状态**（Stage 1/2 都有）与**梯度**（仅 Stage 2）上。u2-l4 讲过引擎侧 `engine.backward` / `engine.step()` 的边界判定，本讲深入 ZeRO 优化器在 `step()` 内部做了什么。

53	## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解
54	
55	### 4.1 IPGBucket：独立并行梯度流水线
56	
57	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
58	
59	朴素数据并行的做法是：反向传播全部结束后，把所有梯度 all-reduce。这在显存和时间上都很浪费——其实反向是逐层生成梯度的，先生成的梯度完全可以先通信。
60	
61	ZeRO-1/2 把这件事做成了一条流水线：反向传播每产生一个参数的梯度，就尝试装进一个**桶**；桶满（累计元素数超过 `reduce_bucket_size`）就立刻发起一次通信。这就是 IPG——每个桶的通信与后续层的反向计算并行执行。
62	
63	`IPGBucket` 是一个 dataclass，记录一个桶的运行时状态。注意构造函数里为**每种通信 dtype 各建一个桶**——因为同一个模型里可能混有 fp16 与 fp32 梯度（例如 autocast 场景），它们不能拼在同一个桶里。
64	
65	#### 4.1.2 核心流程

69	  └─> process_gradients(param)
70	        └─> reduce_independent_p_g_buckets_and_remove_grads(param)
71	              ├─ 若 bucket.elements + param.numel() > reduce_bucket_size:
72	              │     reduce_ipg_grads()          ← 桶满，立刻发起通信
73	              │     overlap_comm 时切换双缓冲 index（0/1 互换）
74	              ├─ contiguous_gradients:
75	              │     把梯度 copy 进桶缓冲的窄视图，grad 指向桶内切片
76	              ├─ MoE 参数：bucket.has_moe_params = True
77	              │     （决定 average_tensor 用哪个进程组）
78	              └─ bucket.elements += param.numel
79	```

157	### 4.2 average_tensor：reduce-scatter 与两种梯度平均模式
158	
159	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
160	
161	桶满后真正执行通信的是 `average_tensor`。它有两个职责：选流与同步（overlap 时在 `reduction_stream` 上执行）、以及把桶内容平均并分发。分发有两种模式，对应配置 `reduce_scatter`：
162	
163	- **all-reduce 模式**（`reduce_scatter=false`）：整个桶做一次带预除的 all-reduce，每个 rank 拿到全量平均梯度，然后各自抽取属于自己的分区。
164	- **reduce-scatter 模式**（`reduce_scatter=true`，默认）：每个 rank 只收到属于自己的那一片平均梯度，通信量是 all-reduce 的 \((N_d-1)/N_d\)，且天然实现 ZeRO-2 的"梯度分区"。
165	
166	MoE 参数有特殊处理：桶内若含 MoE 参数（`bucket.has_moe_params`），该参数的进程组从 `dp_process_group` 换成它所属专家组的 expert data parallel 组。
167	
168	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
169	
170	```
171	average_tensor(tensor, comm_dtype)
172	  ├─ 选流：overlap → reduction_stream（并等待所有生产者流/事件）
173	  ├─ reduce_scatter=false:
174	  │     gradient_reduction_w_predivide(tensor)   ← all-reduce + 预除
175	  │     _add_full_reduction_to_compact_grad_partition(...)
176	  │     return
177	  └─ reduce_scatter=true:
178	        遍历桶内参数，按 partition_ids 计算每个梯度切片的
179	        (目标 rank, 源偏移, 目标偏移, 长度) → rank_and_offsets
180	        按 rank 分组拼接 → 一次 reduce_scatter 完成平均+分区
181	```
182	
183	范数相关的数学：全局 L2 范数按"先局部平方和、再跨组求和、最后开方"计算：
184	
185	\[
186	\|g\|_{\text{global}} = \Big(\sum_{r \in G_{\text{dp}}} \sum_{i \in \text{rank } r} \|g_i\|_2^2\Big)^{1/2}
187	\]
188	
189	这依赖每个元素恰好被一个 rank 持有一份分区——这正是 4.6 节折叠修复要维护的不变量。

273	### 4.4 step / zero_grad：一次优化的完整时序
274	
275	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
276	
277	`step()` 是所有链条的汇合点。它的时序是：**溢出检查 → 全局范数 → （溢出则清空梯度直接返回）→ unscale+clip → 优化器更新本 rank 的 fp32 分区 → fp32 分区降精度写回 bit16 分区 → all-gather 全量参数**。`zero_grad()` 则负责把模型参数上的 `grad`/`grad_accum` 指针清空——注意 ZeRO-2 下大多数参数的梯度在 reduce 后就被丢弃了，只有本分区参数的梯度活到 step。
278	
279	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
280	
281	```
282	step()
283	  ├─ 溢出检查 check_overflow（读各分区的 inf/nan 标记）
284	  ├─ scaled_global_norm()
285	  │     ├─ cpu_offload → complete_grad_norm_calculation_for_cpu_offload
286	  │     └─ 否则 → get_grad_norm_direct(averaged_gradients[i], params_in_partition[i])
287	  ├─ overflow? → zero_grad(set_to_none=True) 并直接 return
288	  ├─ 对每个参数组 i：
289	  │     ├─ flatten：averaged_gradients[i] → single_grad_partition（转 fp32）
290	  │     ├─ unscale_and_clip_grads([single_grad_partition], scaled_global_grad_norm)
291	  │     │     combined_scale = clip * loss_scale
292	  │     │     clip = clamp((norm/loss_scale + 1e-6)/clip_grad, min=1)
293	  │     ├─ _optimizer_step(i)          ← 基础优化器只更新本 rank 分区
294	  │     └─ bit16_partitions[partition_id].copy_(fp32_partition)  ← 降精度写回
295	  └─ all_gather_dp_groups(...)          ← 收回全量参数，供下一轮 forward
296	```
297	
298	裁剪系数的数学：
299	
300	\[
301	c = \frac{\|g\|_{\text{global}} / s + \epsilon}{\tau}, \quad c \leftarrow \max(c, 1), \quad g \leftarrow \frac{g}{c \cdot s}
302	\]
303	
304	其中 \(s\) 是 loss scale，\(\tau\) 是 `gradient_clipping` 阈值，\(\epsilon=10^{-6}\)。\(c \ge 1\) 保证范数小于阈值时不缩放。

347	### 4.5 Adagrad 的 param_groups 重建
348	
349	#### 4.5.1 概念说明
350	
351	大多数优化器（Adam 等）在**第一次 step 时**才惰性创建状态（momentum 等）。但 `torch.optim.Adagrad` 例外：它在**构造时**就为传入的参数初始化 `state`（初始梯度平方和等）。`DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer` 包装基础优化器时，传给基础优化器的是 fp32 分区张量视图；随后 `initialize_optimizer_states` 会给 `single_partition_of_fp32_groups` 挂上 `.grad` 并重建梯度分区。如果此时直接沿用构造期基于旧张量建好的 Adagrad 状态，状态张量会指错设备/张量。
352	
353	修复方式：如果基础优化器是 Adagrad，就用**它自己的 `param_groups`**（而非 fp32 分区张量清单 `single_partition_of_fp32_groups`）连同默认超参重建一个全新的 Adagrad。用 `param_groups` 的关键在于它保留了每个参数组各自的选项（lr、eps 等）与参数身份，重建后状态会在正确的参数（也就是 fp32 分区视图本身）上重新初始化。

360	  │    挂到 single_partition_of_fp32_groups[i].grad（可 pin memory）
361	  └─ if isinstance(optimizer, torch.optim.Adagrad):
362	        optimizer = torch.optim.Adagrad(optimizer.param_groups, **optimizer.defaults)
363	        ← 用参数组（保留每参数组选项）而非分区张量列表重建

387	### 4.6 低精度恢复的 scratch 清零
388	
389	#### 4.6.1 概念说明
390	
391	开启低精度 master（`fp16_master_weights_and_gradients` / `bf16_master_weights_and_grads`，此时 `low_precision_master_weights_and_grads=True`）+ CPU 卸载后，梯度累积发生在 CPU 上，且每个参数只把自己**属于本 rank 分区的那一段**存进 CPU 缓冲（`accumulated_grads_in_cpu[param_id]` 只存分区切片）。在梯度累积边界，`_restore_cpu_offload_grad_to_gpu` 把累积梯度搬回 GPU 供范数计算与溢出检查使用。
392	
393	问题在于搬运目的地 `temp_grad_buffer_for_gpu_offload` 是**所有参数共享的一块 scratch**。低精度模式下只恢复 `num_elements` 长度的分区切片，scratch 里剩下的区域是**上一次某个参数留下的残影**——如果上一步发生过溢出，那里可能还是 NaN。溢出检查读的是"恢复出来的完整梯度"，就会把残留 NaN 误判为本步溢出，造成永远跳步的死循环。
394	
395	修复：恢复前先把整个 scratch 清零（`dest_buffer.zero_()`），再只把有效切片拷进去。
396	
397	#### 4.6.2 核心流程

399	```
400	_restore_cpu_offload_grad_to_gpu(param)
401	  dest_buffer = temp_grad_buffer_for_gpu_offload[:param.numel()]   ← 共享 scratch
402	  if not low_precision:        # 全量恢复，覆盖整块，无残留
403	      dest_buffer.copy_(accumulated_grads_in_cpu[param_id])
404	  else:                        # 分区恢复，scratch 有"无主区域"
405	      dest_buffer.zero_()      # ← 修复点：先清零
406	      dest_buffer[source_offset : source_offset+num_elements].copy_(cpu 累积梯度)
407	  restored = dest_buffer.view_as(param).clone()   # 克隆，scratch 可复用
408	```

452	### 4.7 折叠专家的梯度范数组（本周期修复，PR #8823）
453	
454	#### 4.7.1 概念说明
455	
456	先回顾旧世界（原生 MoE / ETP）的范数计算。`scaled_global_norm` 对每个参数组调 `get_grad_norm_direct`，其中做两级归约：
457	
458	1. 在 DP（或 expert-DP）组上 all-reduce SUM——因为 ZeRO-2 把梯度切到各 rank，每个 rank 只算得到局部平方和；
459	2. 在模型并行组上过滤：只有 `model_parallel_rank == 0`（或 `is_model_parallel_parameter`）的参数计入——因为 TP 复制的参数每个 TP rank 都有相同梯度，全算会重复计数。
460	
461	算完后 `_average_expert_grad_norms` 再对 MoE 参数组做一次"除以 expert-DP world_size 再 all-reduce"的平均。
462	
463	**折叠改变了前提**。AutoEP + AutoTP folding 把专家维折叠进 TP 维：TP 组内的 peers 各持有**不同的路由专家**（参数带 `ds_zero_placement_family = "autoep_expert"` 标记，见 [deepspeed/module_inject/auto_ep_layer.py:L679](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/02f7978481cb3d3297f111c02b16d768b890b256/deepspeed/module_inject/auto_ep_layer.py#L679)）。此时：
464	
465	- 旧路径过滤到 TP rank 0 会**漏掉**非 0 TP rank 持有的专家——这些专家不是复制，是独占的属主；
466	- 专家范数平均也不再成立——折叠组里每个 rank 的范数贡献互不相同，取平均等于丢掉大部分专家的能量。
467	
468	修复后的正确语义（与 [docs/code-docs/source/autoep.rst 的"Gradient clipping under folding"契约](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/02f7978481cb3d3297f111c02b16d768b890b256/docs/code-docs/source/autoep.rst#L609-L625)一致）：折叠专家组的平方范数先在 **expert-DP 分区组**上求和、再在 **EP owner 组**上求和，每个专家属主恰好贡献一次（包括 TP rank 非 0 的属主），且**不再做专家范数平均、不再做 TP 求和**。稠密组与原生 MoE 组保持原路径，两者可在同一优化器中共存。

474	  for 每个参数组 i:
475	    folded = _is_folded_expert_group(i)
476	           = autoep_folding_spec 已配置
477	             且 has_moe_layers

492	           否则 → all_reduce SUM @ expert_parallel_group（折叠新路径）

588	## 6. 本讲小结
589	
590	- ZeRO-1/2 的核心是 **IPG 流水线**：梯度就绪即入桶，桶满即通信（`reduce_ipg_grads`），`overlap_comm` 用双缓冲（`bucket.index` 0/1 切换）让通信与反向重叠；桶大小在"通信次数"与"凑桶延迟"间权衡。
591	- `average_tensor` 有两种模式：`reduce_scatter=true`（默认，一次通信同时完成平均与分区）与 all-reduce + 预除模式；MoE 参数按其 expert-DP 组单独规划切片。
592	- ZeRO-2 的梯度分区可用 `GradPartitionBufferGroup` 紧凑表示：一个 `partition_size` 大小的 fp32 扁平缓冲 + 每参数视图列表，`_zero_padding` 标记让范数计算跳过对齐填充。
593	- `step()` 的固定时序：溢出检查 → 全局范数 → flatten/unscale/clip → 优化器更新 fp32 分区 → 降精度写回 bit16 分区 → all-gather 全量参数；溢出步直接 `zero_grad` 返回。
594	- Adagrad 因**构造期初始化状态**而需要用 `optimizer.param_groups` 重建；低精度 master 从 CPU 恢复梯度前必须 `dest_buffer.zero_()` 清掉共享 scratch 中上一步的 NaN 残影。

# ZeRO-1/2：梯度切分与 IPG 流水线

## 1. 本讲目标

本讲精读 ZeRO Stage 1/2 的核心实现 `DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer`（位于 `deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py`，约 4100 行）。读完本讲你应该能够：

1. 追踪反向传播中梯度的完整旅程：autograd hook → IPG（Independent Parallel Gradients，独立并行梯度）bucket → reduce-scatter / all-reduce → 本 rank 的梯度分区。
2. 解释 `reduce_bucket_size`、`contiguous_gradients`、`overlap_comm`、`reduce_scatter` 这四个配置如何共同决定通信的流水线深度与吞吐。
3. 按顺序定位 `step()` 中 flatten（扁平化）、reduce_scatter、optimizer step、allgather 的调用顺序。
4. 说明 Adagrad 初始化修复：为什么 `initialize_optimizer_states` 要用 `self.optimizer.param_groups`（而不是 fp32 分区张量）重建优化器。
5. 理解低精度 master（`low_precision_master_weights_and_grads`）从 CPU 恢复梯度前先 `dest_buffer.zero_()` 的原因：共享 scratch 中残留的上一步 NaN 会被溢出检查读到。
6. 解读本周期（PR #8823）折叠专家（AutoEP+AutoTP folding）的梯度裁剪修复：`get_grad_norm_direct` 新增 `process_group` / `expert_parallel_group` 参数，`_is_folded_expert_group` 判定出的折叠组范数改为在 expert-DP 分区组与 EP owner 组上求和，且 `_average_expert_grad_norms` 不再对折叠组做专家范数平均。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 ZeRO 三阶段的显存账本

回顾 u5-l1 建立的记号：设模型有 \(\Psi\) 个参数，混合精度训练 + Adam 优化器时每参数的显存开销是：

- 半精度（fp16/bf16）参数：\(2\Psi\) 字节
- 半精度梯度：\(2\Psi\) 字节
- fp32 主权重（master weights）：\(4\Psi\) 字节
- Adam 一阶/二阶矩（各 fp32）：\(8\Psi\) 字节

合计 \(16\Psi\)。朴素数据并行下每个 rank 都完整持有这 \(16\Psi\)。ZeRO 的两级切分：

- **Stage 1**（只切优化器状态）：\(2\Psi + 2\Psi + \dfrac{12\Psi}{N_d}\)
- **Stage 2**（再切梯度）：\(2\Psi + \dfrac{14\Psi}{N_d}\)

其中 \(N_d\) 是数据并行宽度。本讲的 `DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer` 同时承担 Stage 1 和 Stage 2：构造参数 `partition_grads=True` 即 Stage 2，`False` 即 Stage 1。参数始终不切（这是 Stage 3 的事，见 u5-l5）。

### 2.2 关键术语

- **IPG（独立并行梯度）**：不需要等所有梯度生成完毕，反向传播中每凑满一个 bucket 就立刻发起通信，让通信与剩余的反向计算重叠。
- **bucket（桶）**：一组梯度拼接成的通信单元。桶太小则通信次数多、延迟占比高；桶太大则等待凑桶的时间长、峰值显存高。
- **reduce-scatter**：一次集体通信同时完成「求和 + 按 rank 切分结果」，比 all-reduce + 本地切片少一次通信量，是 ZeRO-2 的默认路径。
- **expert data parallel（EDP）组 / expert parallel（EP）组**：MoE 场景下，同一个专家的副本 rank 组成 EDP 组，持有不同专家的 rank 组成 EP 组（详见 u3-l3、u6-l5）。
- **折叠（folding）**：AutoEP + AutoTP 联用时，把专家并行维「折叠」进张量并行维——TP 组内的各 rank 各持**不同**的路由专家。这是理解本讲 4.6 节修复的前提。

### 2.3 与前讲的衔接

u5-l2 讲了 `zero.Init` 如何让参数"从出生就切分"，那是 Stage 3 的入场券。本讲的 Stage 1/2 中参数是完整的，切分只发生在**优化器状态**（Stage 1/2 都有）与**梯度**（仅 Stage 2）上。u2-l4 讲过引擎侧 `engine.backward` / `engine.step()` 的边界判定，本讲深入 ZeRO 优化器在 `step()` 内部做了什么。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 IPGBucket：独立并行梯度流水线

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

朴素数据并行的做法是：反向传播全部结束后，把所有梯度 all-reduce。这在显存和时间上都很浪费——其实反向是逐层生成梯度的，先生成的梯度完全可以先通信。

ZeRO-1/2 把这件事做成了一条流水线：反向传播每产生一个参数的梯度，就尝试装进一个**桶**；桶满（累计元素数超过 `reduce_bucket_size`）就立刻发起一次通信。这就是 IPG——每个桶的通信与后续层的反向计算并行执行。

`IPGBucket` 是一个 dataclass，记录一个桶的运行时状态。注意构造函数里为**每种通信 dtype 各建一个桶**——因为同一个模型里可能混有 fp16 与 fp32 梯度（例如 autocast 场景），它们不能拼在同一个桶里。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```
反向传播（每参数梯度就绪时触发 grad_handling_hook）
  └─> process_gradients(param)
        └─> reduce_independent_p_g_buckets_and_remove_grads(param)
              ├─ 若 bucket.elements + param.numel() > reduce_bucket_size:
              │     reduce_ipg_grads()          ← 桶满，立刻发起通信
              │     overlap_comm 时切换双缓冲 index（0/1 互换）
              ├─ contiguous_gradients:
              │     把梯度 copy 进桶缓冲的窄视图，grad 指向桶内切片
              ├─ MoE 参数：bucket.has_moe_params = True
              │     （决定 average_tensor 用哪个进程组）
              └─ bucket.elements += param.numel
```

桶的通信由 `reduce_ipg_grads` 分派：

- `contiguous_gradients=True`（默认）：直接对桶缓冲的前 `bucket.elements` 个元素做 `average_tensor`；
- `contiguous_gradients=False`：退化为 `_buffered_reduce_fallback`，逐个张量处理非连续梯度。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

1. **实践目标**：直观感受 `reduce_bucket_size` 与 `contiguous_gradients`/`overlap_comm` 组合对每步耗时的影响。
2. **操作步骤**：
   - 准备一个两卡 ZeRO-2 训练脚本（可仿照 `tests/unit/simple_model.py` 的 `SimpleModel`，用 `deepspeed --num_gpus 2` 启动，配置 `zero_optimization.stage=2`、`gradient_clipping=1.0`）。
   - 分别设置 `reduce_bucket_size` 为 \(5\times10^5\)、\(5\times10^6\)、\(5\times10^8\) 各跑 20 步，记录每步平均耗时（`torch.cuda.synchronize()` + 计时）。
   - 再固定一个桶大小，对比 `contiguous_gradients: true/false` × `overlap_comm: true/false` 的四种组合。
3. **需要观察的现象**：桶很小时每步总耗时上升（通信次数多、launch 开销占比大）；桶极大时反向后期的梯度被迫攒着等桶满，重叠机会减少；`contiguous_gradients=false` 时峰值显存通常更高（碎片）。
4. **预期结果**：存在一个中等的桶大小使每步耗时最低；`overlap_comm=true` 时桶的切换使总耗时对桶大小更不敏感。（具体数值依赖硬件，**待本地验证**。）

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么 `ipg_buckets` 是一个以 dtype 为 key 的字典，而不是单个桶？
**答案**：同一模型可能同时存在 fp16 与 fp32 梯度（如 autocast、部分参数强制 fp32），不同 dtype 的张量无法拼进同一块连续缓冲，也无法在一次通信中混用，所以每种通信 dtype 独立成桶（[stage_1_and_2.py:L608-L616](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/02f7978481cb3d3297f111c02b16d768b890b256/deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py#L608-L616)）。

**练习 2**：`bucket.index = 1 - bucket.index` 这行在什么条件下执行、解决什么问题？
**答案**：仅在 `contiguous_gradients and overlap_comm` 时执行（[stage_1_and_2.py:L1432-L1434](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/02f7978481cb3d3297f111c02b16d768b890b256/deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py#L1432-L1434)）。旧桶缓冲正被通信流读取，如果立刻往里写新梯度会数据竞争；双缓冲让下一批梯度写另一块缓冲，读写并行。

**练习 3**：`copy_streams` 字段解决的是什么场景的 bug？
**答案**：torch.compile 下梯度 hook 可能运行在多条 autograd 流上，多条流都向同一个桶拷贝过数据；reduce 流如果只等待当前流，可能读到其他流尚未写完的桶内容（#8061），所以桶记录所有生产者流，`average_tensor` 逐一等待（[stage_1_and_2.py:L1607-L1619](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/02f7978481cb3d3297f111c02b16d768b890b256/deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py#L1607-L1619)）。

### 4.2 average_tensor：reduce-scatter 与两种梯度平均模式

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

桶满后真正执行通信的是 `average_tensor`。它有两个职责：选流与同步（overlap 时在 `reduction_stream` 上执行）、以及把桶内容平均并分发。分发有两种模式，对应配置 `reduce_scatter`：

- **all-reduce 模式**（`reduce_scatter=false`）：整个桶做一次带预除的 all-reduce，每个 rank 拿到全量平均梯度，然后各自抽取属于自己的分区。
- **reduce-scatter 模式**（`reduce_scatter=true`，默认）：每个 rank 只收到属于自己的那一片平均梯度，通信量是 all-reduce 的 \((N_d-1)/N_d\)，且天然实现 ZeRO-2 的"梯度分区"。

MoE 参数有特殊处理：桶内若含 MoE 参数（`bucket.has_moe_params`），该参数的进程组从 `dp_process_group` 换成它所属专家组的 expert data parallel 组。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```
average_tensor(tensor, comm_dtype)
  ├─ 选流：overlap → reduction_stream（并等待所有生产者流/事件）
  ├─ reduce_scatter=false:
  │     gradient_reduction_w_predivide(tensor)   ← all-reduce + 预除
  │     _add_full_reduction_to_compact_grad_partition(...)
  │     return
  └─ reduce_scatter=true:
        遍历桶内参数，按 partition_ids 计算每个梯度切片的
        (目标 rank, 源偏移, 目标偏移, 长度) → rank_and_offsets
        按 rank 分组拼接 → 一次 reduce_scatter 完成平均+分区
```

范数相关的数学：全局 L2 范数按"先局部平方和、再跨组求和、最后开方"计算：

\[
\|g\|_{\text{global}} = \Big(\sum_{r \in G_{\text{dp}}} \sum_{i \in \text{rank } r} \|g_i\|_2^2\Big)^{1/2}
\]

这依赖每个元素恰好被一个 rank 持有一份分区——这正是 4.6 节折叠修复要维护的不变量。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

流选择与多生产者等待：

[deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py:L1597-L1628](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/02f7978481cb3d3297f111c02b16d768b890b256/deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py#L1597-L1628)

非 reduce-scatter 路径在这里提前返回（第 1625-1628 行），走 `gradient_reduction_w_predivide` 的 all-reduce。

reduce-scatter 的切片规划：

[deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py:L1630-L1663](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/02f7978481cb3d3297f111c02b16d768b890b256/deepspeed/runtime/zero/stage_1_and_2.py#L1630-L1663)

注意第 1647-1649 行：桶里有 MoE 参数时，MoE 参数用其专家组的 expert-DP 组、稠密参数仍用 DP 组——一次 reduce_scatter 只能在一个组上做，所以这里按参数逐个确定组并规划切片。

### 4.3 GradPartitionBufferGroup：紧凑梯度分区缓冲

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

ZeRO-2 中每个 rank 最终只需要持有自己那份梯度分区。如果 `gradient_accumulation_dtype` 是 fp32 且与参数 dtype 不同（最典型的：fp16/bf16 训练 + fp32 梯度累积），梯度分区可以做成一个**恰好 partition_size 大小的紧凑 fp32 缓冲**，reduce-scatter 的结果直接落进对应切片，不需要任何中间拷贝。`GradPartitionBufferGroup` 就是这个缓冲：它是一个 `list` 子类——列表元素是每个参数对应的缓冲视图（保持与参数一一对应，便于按参数求范数、清零），同时持有 `flat_partition`（底层一维大张量）。

   条件: gradient_accumulation_dtype == fp32 且 != 参数 dtype，

是 → _build_compact_grad_partition_buffer(i):
      flat_partition = zeros(partition_size, dtype=fp32)
      按参数在分区中的 (dest_offset, num_elements) 切窄视图，
      视图形状还原为参数形状；空隙标记 _zero_padding=True
      → GradPartitionBufferGroup(views, flat_partition)
否 → 传统路径: averaged_gradients[i] = get_flat_partition(...)
```

### 4.4 step / zero_grad：一次优化的完整时序

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

`step()` 是所有链条的汇合点。它的时序是：**溢出检查 → 全局范数 → （溢出则清空梯度直接返回）→ unscale+clip → 优化器更新本 rank 的 fp32 分区 → fp32 分区降精度写回 bit16 分区 → all-gather 全量参数**。`zero_grad()` 则负责把模型参数上的 `grad`/`grad_accum` 指针清空——注意 ZeRO-2 下大多数参数的梯度在 reduce 后就被丢弃了，只有本分区参数的梯度活到 step。

#### 4.4.2 核心流程

```
step()
  ├─ 溢出检查 check_overflow（读各分区的 inf/nan 标记）
  ├─ scaled_global_norm()
  │     ├─ cpu_offload → complete_grad_norm_calculation_for_cpu_offload
  │     └─ 否则 → get_grad_norm_direct(averaged_gradients[i], params_in_partition[i])
  ├─ overflow? → zero_grad(set_to_none=True) 并直接 return
  ├─ 对每个参数组 i：
  │     ├─ flatten：averaged_gradients[i] → single_grad_partition（转 fp32）
  │     ├─ unscale_and_clip_grads([single_grad_partition], scaled_global_grad_norm)
  │     │     combined_scale = clip * loss_scale
  │     │     clip = clamp((norm/loss_scale + 1e-6)/clip_grad, min=1)
  │     ├─ _optimizer_step(i)          ← 基础优化器只更新本 rank 分区
  │     └─ bit16_partitions[partition_id].copy_(fp32_partition)  ← 降精度写回
  └─ all_gather_dp_groups(...)          ← 收回全量参数，供下一轮 forward
```

裁剪系数的数学：

\[
c = \frac{\|g\|_{\text{global}} / s + \epsilon}{\tau}, \quad c \leftarrow \max(c, 1), \quad g \leftarrow \frac{g}{c \cdot s}
\]

其中 \(s\) 是 loss scale，\(\tau\) 是 `gradient_clipping` 阈值，\(\epsilon=10^{-6}\)。\(c \ge 1\) 保证范数小于阈值时不缩放。

### 4.5 Adagrad 的 param_groups 重建

#### 4.5.1 概念说明

大多数优化器（Adam 等）在**第一次 step 时**才惰性创建状态（momentum 等）。但 `torch.optim.Adagrad` 例外：它在**构造时**就为传入的参数初始化 `state`（初始梯度平方和等）。`DeepSpeedZeroOptimizer` 包装基础优化器时，传给基础优化器的是 fp32 分区张量视图；随后 `initialize_optimizer_states` 会给 `single_partition_of_fp32_groups` 挂上 `.grad` 并重建梯度分区。如果此时直接沿用构造期基于旧张量建好的 Adagrad 状态，状态张量会指错设备/张量。

修复方式：如果基础优化器是 Adagrad，就用**它自己的 `param_groups`**（而非 fp32 分区张量清单 `single_partition_of_fp32_groups`）连同默认超参重建一个全新的 Adagrad。用 `param_groups` 的关键在于它保留了每个参数组各自的选项（lr、eps 等）与参数身份，重建后状态会在正确的参数（也就是 fp32 分区视图本身）上重新初始化。

#### 4.5.2 核心流程

```
initialize_optimizer_states()
  ├─ 为每组 i 构造 single_grad_partition（partition_size 大小的零张量）
  │    挂到 single_partition_of_fp32_groups[i].grad（可 pin memory）
  └─ if isinstance(optimizer, torch.optim.Adagrad):
        optimizer = torch.optim.Adagrad(optimizer.param_groups, **optimizer.defaults)
        ← 用参数组（保留每参数组选项）而非分区张量列表重建
```

### 4.6 低精度恢复的 scratch 清零

#### 4.6.1 概念说明

开启低精度 master（`fp16_master_weights_and_gradients` / `bf16_master_weights_and_grads`，此时 `low_precision_master_weights_and_grads=True`）+ CPU 卸载后，梯度累积发生在 CPU 上，且每个参数只把自己**属于本 rank 分区的那一段**存进 CPU 缓冲（`accumulated_grads_in_cpu[param_id]` 只存分区切片）。在梯度累积边界，`_restore_cpu_offload_grad_to_gpu` 把累积梯度搬回 GPU 供范数计算与溢出检查使用。

问题在于搬运目的地 `temp_grad_buffer_for_gpu_offload` 是**所有参数共享的一块 scratch**。低精度模式下只恢复 `num_elements` 长度的分区切片，scratch 里剩下的区域是**上一次某个参数留下的残影**——如果上一步发生过溢出，那里可能还是 NaN。溢出检查读的是"恢复出来的完整梯度"，就会把残留 NaN 误判为本步溢出，造成永远跳步的死循环。

修复：恢复前先把整个 scratch 清零（`dest_buffer.zero_()`），再只把有效切片拷进去。

#### 4.6.2 核心流程

```
_restore_cpu_offload_grad_to_gpu(param)
  dest_buffer = temp_grad_buffer_for_gpu_offload[:param.numel()]   ← 共享 scratch
  if not low_precision:        # 全量恢复，覆盖整块，无残留
      dest_buffer.copy_(accumulated_grads_in_cpu[param_id])
  else:                        # 分区恢复，scratch 有"无主区域"
      dest_buffer.zero_()      # ← 修复点：先清零
      dest_buffer[source_offset : source_offset+num_elements].copy_(cpu 累积梯度)
  restored = dest_buffer.view_as(param).clone()   # 克隆，scratch 可复用
```

### 4.7 折叠专家的梯度范数组（本周期修复，PR #8823）

#### 4.7.1 概念说明

先回顾旧世界（原生 MoE / ETP）的范数计算。`scaled_global_norm` 对每个参数组调 `get_grad_norm_direct`，其中做两级归约：

1. 在 DP（或 expert-DP）组上 all-reduce SUM——因为 ZeRO-2 把梯度切到各 rank，每个 rank 只算得到局部平方和；
2. 在模型并行组上过滤：只有 `model_parallel_rank == 0`（或 `is_model_parallel_parameter`）的参数计入——因为 TP 复制的参数每个 TP rank 都有相同梯度，全算会重复计数。

算完后 `_average_expert_grad_norms` 再对 MoE 参数组做一次"除以 expert-DP world_size 再 all-reduce"的平均。

**折叠改变了前提**。AutoEP + AutoTP folding 把专家维折叠进 TP 维：TP 组内的 peers 各持有**不同的路由专家**（参数带 `ds_zero_placement_family = "autoep_expert"` 标记，见 [deepspeed/module_inject/auto_ep_layer.py:L679](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/02f7978481cb3d3297f111c02b16d768b890b256/deepspeed/module_inject/auto_ep_layer.py#L679)）。此时：

- 旧路径过滤到 TP rank 0 会**漏掉**非 0 TP rank 持有的专家——这些专家不是复制，是独占的属主；
- 专家范数平均也不再成立——折叠组里每个 rank 的范数贡献互不相同，取平均等于丢掉大部分专家的能量。

修复后的正确语义（与 [docs/code-docs/source/autoep.rst 的"Gradient clipping under folding"契约](https://github.com/deepspeedai/DeepSpeed/blob/02f7978481cb3d3297f111c02b16d768b890b256/docs/code-docs/source/autoep.rst#L609-L625)一致）：折叠专家组的平方范数先在 **expert-DP 分区组**上求和、再在 **EP owner 组**上求和，每个专家属主恰好贡献一次（包括 TP rank 非 0 的属主），且**不再做专家范数平均、不再做 TP 求和**。稠密组与原生 MoE 组保持原路径，两者可在同一优化器中共存。

#### 4.7.2 核心流程

```
scaled_global_norm()
  for 每个参数组 i:
    folded = _is_folded_expert_group(i)
           = autoep_folding_spec 已配置
             且 has_moe_layers
             且 is_moe_param_group[i]
             且组内所有参数 ds_zero_placement_family == "autoep_expert"
    if folded:
        group_name = optimizer.param_groups[i]["name"]
        norm = get_grad_norm_direct(...,
                 process_group=real_dp_process_group[i],   ← expert-DP 分区组
                 expert_parallel_group=ep_process_group[group_name]) ← EP owner 组
    else:
        norm = get_grad_norm_direct(...)                   ← 原路径

get_grad_norm_direct(gradients, params, norm_type, process_group, expert_parallel_group)
  局部: total = Σ_i ‖g_i‖²（折叠组不过滤 TP rank 0，全部计入）
  第 1 级: all_reduce SUM @ process_group（默认 dp_process_group）
  第 2 级: expert_parallel_group 为 None → _model_parallel_all_reduce（原路径）
           否则 → all_reduce SUM @ expert_parallel_group（折叠新路径）

_average_expert_grad_norms(norm_groups)
  仅对 is_moe_param_group[i] 且【非折叠组】做平均
```

折叠组的范数数学（每个属主恰好一次）：

\[
\|g_E\|^2 = \sum_{o \in G_{\text{EP}}} \; \sum_{r \in G_{\text{EDP}}(o)} \; \sum_{i \in \text{partition}(r)} \|g_i\|_2^2
\]

## 6. 本讲小结

- ZeRO-1/2 的核心是 **IPG 流水线**：梯度就绪即入桶，桶满即通信（`reduce_ipg_grads`），`overlap_comm` 用双缓冲（`bucket.index` 0/1 切换）让通信与反向重叠；桶大小在"通信次数"与"凑桶延迟"间权衡。
- `average_tensor` 有两种模式：`reduce_scatter=true`（默认，一次通信同时完成平均与分区）与 all-reduce + 预除模式；MoE 参数按其 expert-DP 组单独规划切片。
- ZeRO-2 的梯度分区可用 `GradPartitionBufferGroup` 紧凑表示：一个 `partition_size` 大小的 fp32 扁平缓冲 + 每参数视图列表，`_zero_padding` 标记让范数计算跳过对齐填充。
- `step()` 的固定时序：溢出检查 → 全局范数 → flatten/unscale/clip → 优化器更新 fp32 分区 → 降精度写回 bit16 分区 → all-gather 全量参数；溢出步直接 `zero_grad` 返回。
- Adagrad 因**构造期初始化状态**而需要用 `optimizer.param_groups` 重建；低精度 master 从 CPU 恢复梯度前必须 `dest_buffer.zero_()` 清掉共享 scratch 中上一步的 NaN 残影。
- 本周期折叠专家修复（#8823）：`get_grad_norm_direct` 参数化归约组，折叠专家组（`ds_zero_placement_family` 全为 `autoep_expert`）的范数在 expert-DP 分区组与 EP owner 组上级联求和、跳过 TP rank 0 过滤、豁免专家范数平均；稠密组与原生 MoE 组保持原路径并可共存。

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

schema.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
